text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
FormOf(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.

Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
FormOf(cholangiocarcinoma, bileDuctCancer) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
FormOf(bileDuctCancer, cancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a form of cancer.
FormOf(mildFlu, flu) ::: Mild flu is a form of flu.
FormOf(colorectalCancer, cancer) ::: Colorectal cancer is a form of cancer.
¬(FormOf(colorectalCancer, bileDuctCancer) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(colorectalCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.

Conclusion:
((FormOf(colorectalCancer, bileDuctCancer) ∨ FormOf(colorectalCancer, cholangiocarcinoma)) → (FormOf(colorectalCancer, bileDuctCancer) ∧ FormOf(colorectalCancer, mildFlu))) ::: If colorectal cancer is a kind of bile duct cancer or a form of Cholangiocarcinoma, then colorectal cancer is a kind of bile duct cancer and a kind of mild flu.
